objective: Difficulty probe, not a cohort. v0.9 ran text-redact for 40 paid rollouts without ever having run it against a model, and it saturated at 39 of 40 with its code point hazard never firing once. redact-spans is the same behavioral contract with the hazard no longer telegraphed in the instruction and with more hidden cases able to catch a wrong string unit. It carries a new family id because it is a different task, and text-redact is left untouched so the v0.9 result stays reproducible. This probe measures whether redact-spans is hard enough to be worth a cohort block.

analysis.primary_estimand: count of passing rollouts out of ten, and the count of rollouts failing at least one of the five hidden cases that a wrong string unit breaks: code-point-offsets, astral-mask, astral-literal-scan, merge-touching, min-length-drops-before-merge
analysis.uncertainty: None reported. Ten rollouts cannot estimate a pass rate and this probe does not try to. It is a go/no-go on the family.
analysis.stopping_rule: Fixed at 10 rollouts, two per language, written down before the first paid call. No continuation on observed results. If the answer is ambiguous the family is revised, not sampled further.

admission_rule: Admit text-redact v1.0 to a cohort only if it passes at most 7 of 10 AND at least 1 rollout fails a wrong-unit hidden case. Both conditions must hold. Passing 8 or more means the family saturates again. Passing few but never failing a wrong-unit case means the difficulty is coming from somewhere other than the hazard the family exists to test, which is a different task and needs a different justification.
notes: These rollouts are a go/no-go on the task and are never pooled into a reported cohort result. The cohort that admits this family must rerun it with its own seeds. The free calibration gate is green for redact-spans and the untouched starter fails eleven of thirteen checks; that is what makes the scoring fair and says nothing about difficulty, which is the whole reason this probe exists.

execution.note: text-redact is command-mode, so contention does not touch correctness, agent steps, or cost. Wall-clock time is not an outcome here.
